stories.headline: Kevin named his team after Adam and drew him in week one
stories.body:
The schedule did this on its own. #CrookedAdam, the team Kevin built and named after another man in this league, opens the season against Coker? I hardly know her!, the team that man actually runs. Of all eleven opponents available, the calendar handed him that one first.

Adam leads 20.42 to nothing. Not because he has played well, particularly, but because he owned two New England players in the only game that has kicked off and Kevin owned none. Drake Maye was projected for 19.7 and returned 14.82 despite throwing three interceptions. A.J. Brown was projected for 16.8 and returned 5.60 before an ankle injury ended his night in the second half.

Kevin has nine starters still to play and the second best projected roster in the league at 124.4 a week. This lead will not survive Sunday afternoon. It is, for the next seventy-two hours, the funniest number on the site.
stories.storyline: Kevin, whose team is named #CrookedAdam, plays Adam head to head in week 1. Adam led 20.42 to 0.00 after Wednesday. Open question: whether the grudge team beats the man it is named after.

takes.text: Twelve teams, eleven possible opponents, and the schedule looked at the man who named his roster after a rival and said: week one. I did not think this league was capable of narrative. I was wrong and I am delighted.

Worth stating plainly that a 20.42 to nothing lead after one Wednesday game means nothing at all. Kevin has nine starters yet to play against Adam's seven. If you projected the rest out, Kevin wins this comfortably more often than not.

I do not care that it is Wednesday. Kevin spent an entire offseason building a monument to a grudge, and the first time the man is standing in front of him, he puts up a zero. A zero! You do not get to name the team after somebody and then not show up.

Adam has 17.4 percent of his projected weekly total already banked. Kevin has zero percent of his. That gap is entirely about which NFL teams played on Wednesday and contains no information about either roster.

stories.headline: Jerey leads the league on the back of one receiver, and he is playing the team least equipped to answer
stories.body:
Kamara Sutra has 35.50 points, more than any other team in Sigma Pi B, and 26.20 of that is Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Projected for 19.7, he delivered the largest overperformance of the night by a distance, piling up most of his yardage in the fourth quarter while Seattle came back to win.

Jerey had three players in the opener and the other two roughly cancelled out. Andy Borregales, his best value pick of the draft at 167, kicked for 6.00 against a 6.1 projection. AJ Barner went for 3.30 against 9.3, the second worst return of the night.

His opponent is Jeff, who has zero points, the lowest projected roster in the league at 108.0, the worst draft grade at negative 12.5 per pick, and 10 percent playoff odds. Jeff also has all nine starters still to play, which is the only encouraging sentence available to him.
stories.storyline: Jerey leads week 1 at 35.50 on the strength of Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 26.20. He faces Jeff, who is projected last in the league. Open question: whether the lowest-projected roster can cover a 35 point head start.

takes.text: Smith-Njigba put up 26.20 with a backup quarterback throwing to him after Darnold went down on the opening drive. That is not a good fantasy performance, that is a player carrying a franchise on national television. Jerey did nothing to deserve him and he has him anyway.

One receiver is 74 percent of Jerey's total, which is the least stable way to hold a lead in this sport. He also started the second worst performer of the night in Barner. The league table currently ranks nobody. It ranks who had Seattle players.
Jeff is losing by thirty-five points to a man whose kicker outscored his tight end. And Jeff has not even played yet. That is the year he is having and it is Thursday.

I want to defend Jerey's kicker, briefly, because nobody else will. Andy Borregales at pick 167 was the best value selection on his roster by our measure, and he returned essentially exactly what he was projected to. That is what a late kicker is for.

stories.headline: The tightest game in the league is a backup running back against a kicker
stories.body:
Scheme leads Baltimore Boofers 7.80 to 7.00. Every point on the board comes from two players. Justin's is Jadarian Price, a Seattle running back projected for 9.8 who returned 7.80. Jake's is Jason Myers, who kicked the go-ahead field goal with 5:50 remaining and returned 7.00 against a 6.9 projection.

That is the entire game so far. Two rosters projecting a combined 230 points a week, separated by eight tenths of a point, contributed by a committee back and a placekicker.

Jake needs this one. His projected strength fell from 120.0 to 108.8 over the past week and his playoff odds went with it, from 39 percent down to 13. He is now projected eleventh of twelve, having entered the season tenth.
stories.storyline: Jake's projected strength fell from 120.0 to 108.8 and his playoff odds from 39 percent to 13 without playing a game. Open question: whether the collapse reflects real roster damage or a projection correction.

takes.text: Both of these teams project over 108 points a week and have produced 14.80 between them. That is the correct way to read a Thursday scoreboard: it is not a measurement of anything, it is a measurement of the NFL schedule.

Jason Myers won an actual football game on Wednesday night and has delivered seven points and a thirteen percent playoff chance. Kicking is the only job in America where you can be perfect and still be the reason people are worried about you.

Thirteen percent! Jake has gone from thirty-nine to thirteen in a week without losing a game, and his answer to it was a kicker doing exactly what kickers do. Somebody get this man on the waiver wire.

The Jake situation deserves care rather than mockery. A drop of 11.2 projected points a week usually means something concrete happened to a starter, and it happened between two readings of the same week. That is worth understanding before anyone writes him off.

stories.headline: Killian and Brian are tied at nothing, and four desks already called it
stories.body:
Team Ketchup against Team Mountain is 0.00 to 0.00. Neither roster had a player in Wednesday's game.

Killian arrived at that zero having lost more ground than anyone. A week ago he projected 128.3 a week, the best in the league, with 73 percent playoff odds and the top seed favourite's tag. He now projects 114.7, which is tenth of twelve, with 34 percent odds. He has not played a snap or made a transaction.

Every desk on this panel doubted that original number in print. Deacon called it a computer that had watched zero football. Odessa called it a list in a plausible order rather than a ranking. Roy awarded an invisible trophy. Ward, who had Killian second on his own ballot, still described him as a fine favourite and a weak one. All four are on the record and all four were right within a week.

Elsewhere, one prediction remains stubbornly unresolved. Kyler Murray, whom Chris drafted at 178 and released before the season, does not appear on a single roster in this league. Twelve managers have now had a full week to claim a starting quarterback and none of them have.
stories.storyline: Killian fell from 128.3 and first to 114.7 and tenth without playing, losing 39 points of playoff odds. Kyler Murray remains unclaimed on every roster in the league. Open questions: whether Killian's collapse is real, and whether anyone eventually signs Murray.

takes.text: Four days. That is how long the best team in Sigma Pi B lasted. Not one snap, not one lineup decision, not one mistake by the manager. A spreadsheet changed its mind and the era ended.

I will take the receipt and then complain about it, because someone should. A projection that can move 13.6 points a week in four days is not precise enough to have been published as a ranking in the first place, and I published it. The lesson is not that Killian is bad. It is that early September numbers deserve error bars nobody ever prints.

I would add one caution to our victory lap. We doubted the ranking, which was correct, but nothing that has happened on a football field has told us anything about Killian's team yet. He is 0.00 in a 0.00 game. Being right about a projection is not the same as being right about a roster.

Kyler Murray has now been available to this entire league for a full week. A starting quarterback. Free. Nobody wants him. I have watched twelve grown men look directly at a functioning NFL starter and collectively decide they would rather not.
